source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: A busy morning at the supermarket checkout line. Shoppers line up in long lines, their faces aglow with excitement. They're pushing past shelves, picking items up on carts. A cashier stands at the front, carefully counting out change. Nearby, shoppers stand still to read their receipts. In the back, a conveyor belt moves with its rhythmic clicks and hum. Inside, there’s a cool, steady beep that announces the totals of each purchase. Below, cards scan passersby through the safety gates. In the center, a register records every transaction. A shoplifter makes a quick exit, leaving behind a few loose bits of plastic and paper scraps. The store smells faintly of stale cheese and stale bread. And then, suddenly, it's quiet again, as if everyone has decided to stop shopping today.

In the bustling supermarket checkout line at the busiest hour, where the aisles were packed like a never-ending maze, the sound of scurrying feet mingled with the soft hum of electronic beepers. A single shopper had been pushed past a queue so crowded they seemed to have vanished beneath the conveyor belts. The cart was heavy but steady as always, carrying boxes that clattered across the counter top. The shelves were filled with a variety of products—fruits, vegetables, bread, and dairy goods. The cash registers beeped loudly, but not with the usual enthusiasm. The temperature inside the store was consistently high—warmth emanated from various appliances throughout the day.

As the cashier scanned each item, she began her daily routine, making sure every transaction went off without a hitch. With a practiced grace, she pulled out a small plastic bin, carefully placed it on the side of the aisle, and walked back towards the checkout lane. Behind her, a lone shopper took stock of what he might have missed, his face obscured by the folds of his shopping bags. His eyes were wide with wonder, as he looked around, looking for something—a product he had overlooked before. The shopper sighed, feeling slightly guilty for being so late, knowing he would now have to make do with whatever remained in his cart. As he made his way through the lines, he couldn't help but feel grateful for the simplicity of things today, especially when faced with a rush hour like today's.

The tension between the cashier and the shopper was palpable as they waited their turn to be checked out. The cashier smiled softly, patting the shoulder of the lone shopper who nodded slowly, indicating that he had made it through one more line, leaving just enough room for the next one. The customer was about to place the last item on the receipt, but his expression changed suddenly. He paused, looking down at his watch, then turned back to look at the cashier. "It'll be two minutes," he said, his voice barely above a whisper, as though the weight of time were weighing heavily on him.

The cashier, noticing the change in demeanor, cleared her throat and asked if there were any special reasons for the extended wait. The lone shopper nodded again, looking visibly uncomfortable, and explained that he had forgotten some items after arriving in such large quantities. The cashier examined his face closely, trying to gauge how much effort he had expended, then said, "I understand, I've got to be careful about losing them." She then handed the receipt to him and asked if he needed anything else, prompting him to glance back and forth in his direction.

As he continued on his way, the cashier noticed a sign posted near the exit—their name on it, which led her directly to the checkout. Before leaving, she gave him another chance to pay, offering to assist him if necessary. The lone shopper was grateful for the extra assistance, and as they exited the building, the scent of fruit and cheese filled the air, a welcome relief from the long queues. The shopkeeper, who had been counting the tips since closing, quickly brought the final amount of money into payment, then thanked the clerk profusely for everything she'd done so far today. As the customer made his way home, he felt a sense of completion, knowing that his purchase, whether groceries or other treats, would be honored. The checkout line faded away, revealing a peaceful scene of shoppers walking past, enjoying each other's company, and the gentle breeze carrying the fresh scent of their morning meals.

In the bustling supermarket checkout line at the busiest time of day, the conveyor belt hummed with activity, the barcode scanners gleamed with digital light, and bags clattered along the conveyor belts like tiny, metallic chains. Shoppers swirled around in the aisles, their faces painted shades of red and yellow, each one holding what they thought would make them happy, their minds filled with excitement and anticipation. 

A young man, his eyes scanning the shelves with determination, scanned through a large, colorful section of groceries, his fingers dancing across the plastic labels. Behind him, a woman, her face obscured by a hood, looked on in bemusement as she counted the items on the register. A child, with bright red hair and brown eyes, stood near the cash register, clutching a small package and looking expectantly back towards the shoppers.

As the shop emptied itself out onto the street, the store manager walked past, carrying his merchandise in one hand and a clipboard in the other. "Good afternoon, everyone," he said, his voice low and familiar, "how do we keep our prices competitive in this market?"

The shoppers exchanged glances, not knowing what else to say but to exchange pleasantries. The elderly lady nearby handed a few items to a younger patron, who took them eagerly and started rummaging through the rest of the case. The mother of two, her arms laden with grocery sacks, watched in silence while the children played peek-a-boo under a tree outside the store, oblivious to the noise that permeated every moment of the shift.

Outside, in the dimly lit parking lot, a car with its horn blaring pulled into the store, taking the place of the lone vehicle in the aisle. As the owner of the car stepped out, he was greeted by a wave of approval from the employees inside. "Thank you so much for bringing us such high-quality products, sir!" he exclaimed, extending an arm. "We appreciate it!"

With a grin, the salesman moved forward to greet the new customer, explaining how everything in the store was sold out before it closed. As the salesperson walked away, the clerk with the clipboard sat down beside her, checking to see if there were any last-minute changes to the price lists. "Just a minute," she called out to a customer standing nearby. "Have you checked out yet?" She tapped her phone on her desk and then dialed the number of the nearest store.

Hours passed, shoppers continued to move through the aisles, their pace almost impossible to follow without paying attention to the signs and advertisements surrounding them. At one point, a group of customers began talking loudly on their cell phones, causing the entire store to become a mess of noise. One woman approached the counter and placed a bill of five dollars down, looking anxious. Her partner followed closely, tapping the cash register anxiously.

Suddenly, a loud boom reverberated throughout the store, startling the staff and making everyone freeze. They looked around, searching for the sound source, but saw nothing until they realized it came from the cashier in the far corner. He had just finished counting the remaining goods when he heard a commotion coming from the next aisle. "What's wrong?" he asked the attendant, a hint of urgency in his voice. "I'm sorry, sir."

The employee turned around and saw the source, but was too late. The cashier had already grabbed two more bags from the counter, hurriedly stuffing them down the back of the suitcases before turning toward the exit. As the cashier walked away, the attendant, visibly shaken, reached out to touch the cash register, but could not quite pull herself away.

Minutes later, a long, drawn-out beep sounded through the store. The sound echoed through the aisles, causing many people to look up, their eyes wide. Finally, after several moments of silence, the salesperson finally managed to gather the necessary information. "So, did anyone get a deal today?" she asked, trying to sound as normal as possible. "Well, yes and no," came the response from the manager behind the counter. "There wasn't really a big sale, though." He paused, looking at the list of items available. "Let me count it myself, shall we? I've got $28 left!"

One shopper, wearing dark blue jeans and a black sweatshirt, stepped forward, her bag slung over her shoulder. "I'm sorry," she said softly. "It seems like someone went missing."

The security guard, standing at the cash register, raised an eyebrow. "That's odd, isn't it?" he mused aloud. But before he could continue, a sudden commotion outside the store caused him to freeze. The crowd that had been gathered around the cash register began to scatter, leaving no sign of their original purpose.

"Shut up," the guard shouted at a passing worker. "This isn't the right place to talk about things like that! We have our rules!"

In the bustling aisles of the supermarket checkout line, customers waited anxiously for their next shopping adventure. With each purchase, they scanned the scanners, filled out receipts, and checked the shelves, often feeling a wave of anticipation wash over them during long lines. In the corner, a young woman stood amidst the chaos, her bags heavy but purposeful, her eyes never leaving the display of products. She was the cashier, her presence soothing the anxious shoppers. Behind her, a tall man took his turn on a conveyor belt, the beep of the machine barely muffled by the clatter of feet. Another shopper, with a delicate clipboard tucked inside his pocket, crowded the aisles like invisible dust. A cart held everything he needed without hesitation, the divider bar served as a makeshift scale, its edges sharp and visible underfoot. As the clock ticked down, the cashier counted every item, ensuring nothing slipped through the cracks. Loyalty cards appeared at the side of the line, a digital note that promised rewards if enough purchases were made. In a moment, the total announced, and the cashier beamed proudly, his face reflecting genuine satisfaction and perhaps a glint of hope. And so, in the midst of the hustle and bustle, shoppers took their seats, ready to embrace the challenges ahead.

In the bustling supermarket checkout lane, amidst the clatter and commotion, the human scent was the most dominant, carried not just by the workers but also by the shoppers' breath and sweat. In the center of the aisles, the cashiers stood tall, their uniforms blending seamlessly into the background; they were the invisible guardians of the store's financial records. As the sun dipped lower, casting long shadows across the floor, a small figure stood out against the backdrop of the crowds, his name a mystery, yet he appeared to be one of those rare exceptions who seemed to have found a way through this overwhelming chaos.

The conveyor belt whirred past them at a steady pace, its grooves honed into smooth, polished edges. Each part of it played its role, ensuring that everything moved smoothly without incident. But what really intrigued them was the bagging area, where each piece of merchandise was meticulously sorted by weight before being placed on display at the counter. The cashier, with her keen eyes and sharp mind, worked tirelessly to make sure every item was spot-on. Her smile, ever-present despite her years of experience, gave the impression of a beacon of hope, guiding the shoppers through the bewildering array of goods they had just bought.

Behind the counter, another shopper was pushing a cart full of groceries, his face etched with impatience as he navigated around the frayed perimeter. A single tear had slipped down his cheek, perhaps from standing so long in one place. He looked at his watch in bewilderment as he approached the cash register. His heart was pounding, driven by the anticipation of a quick sale or a special promotion. This was a day filled with unexpected opportunities.

Then came the moment when the little friction caught him off guard—a sudden jolt as if someone had knocked something onto the countertop. The cashier, her eyes widening in surprise, took note of the noise and quickly checked the display for the specific product, trying to remember its brand and the quantity needed. Her rapid movements and cautious approach ensured that the customer did not feel rushed or abandoned.

As the checkout continued, the register began to beep incessantly, signaling the end of the shopping trip. The total declared by the cashier—$500.12—was announced proudly on the screen next to the cart, making it easy for the cashier to calculate the final bill, even though the amount seemed like a distant memory after all these days of hard work.

With the last payment made, the cashier stepped back to check the display, then hurriedly walked away to gather change and return to the register for the transaction. The entire scene was punctuated by the occasional beep from the cashier’s phone as she tried to retrieve her data for the night shift. She glanced at the customer, smiling slightly, then turned towards the counter, ready to complete the final tally.

It was a slow morning, a reminder that the world was always changing, bringing new experiences and opportunities. But amidst the hustle and bustle, there was always one thing—the warmth of a good laugh and the satisfaction of knowing one had managed to fit into the supermarket, whether that meant buying a few things that never got used or simply enjoying the peace and quiet of a well-kept store.

In a bustling supermarket checkout line at a busy hour, customers lined up eagerly, their faces full of anticipation and nervousness. Another customer, wearing a black shirt and cargo pants, pushed some items onto the scale, clearly stressed about weighing them correctly.

Later in the checkout area, the cashier turned to the elderly man and asked if everything was alright. He nodded, smiling slightly, then handed her a piece of paper with details of today's sales. One shopper commented, "I can't believe how long those people were waiting... maybe I should check in on them sometime," and another said, "I just want to make sure everyone has what they need."

As the day concluded, the checkout line slowly emptied, leaving fewer customers standing than before. But even in our busy city of stores, there's still time to enjoy a good bargain!
